note: GROUPING DELIMITERS ADDED - NEEDS HUMAN AUDIT. The parentheses around the two-term factor (1/r^2 - r/R^3) are NOT visible in the crop image: the page renders a blank gap on each side of the factor instead of a bracket glyph. They are included here because the delimiters are structurally present in the typesetting - each side is a three-piece extensible Symbol-font parenthesis whose pieces all map to U+0020 and therefore paint nothing - and the visible gaps in the image sit exactly where those pieces are placed (one gap between the 4 pi epsilon_0 fraction and 1/r^2, one between r/R^3 and the semicolon). A strictly glyph-faithful reading would give 'E(r) = Ze/(4 pi epsilon_0) * 1/r^2 - r/R^3', which is a different expression: without the delimiters the final term detaches from the prefactor. I chose the typeset structure over the rendered-blank appearance so the LaTeX does not read as mathematically different from the printed equation; nothing was computed, simplified or rearranged, and the delimiters are parentheses because that is the glyph family actually present, not square brackets. If the audit prefers literal glyph fidelity, drop the \left( and \right). Also excluded as outside target_box_in_crop: a clipped 'R^3' fragment at the top edge of the crop, the preceding line 'Gauss's law then gives,', and all following prose and equations beginning 'The electric field is directed radially outward.' - these belong to neighbouring blocks.
